title: Feasibility of reduced PTV margins in magnetic resonance image-guided online adaptive radiotherapy for bladder cancer: a personalised approach

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Feasibility of reduced PTV margins in magnetic resonance image-guided online adaptive radiotherapy for bladder cancer: a personalised approach》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0020】Bladder radiotherapy offers an organ-preserving treatment option for those with bladder cancer [1], [2]. By convention, the whole bladder is irradiated. However, the bladder presents a complex target for radiotherapy, posing inter- and intra-fractional deformations due to urinary filling and displacement by adjacent organs [3], [4], [5]. This variability is influenced by patient-specific factors, including hydration, extent of disease, urinary function and individual anatomy [3], [4], [5], [6], [7]. Historically, this uncertainty has been accounted for with extensive population-based planning target volume (PTV) margins, at the expense of normal tissue irradiation [3], [4], [5].

【Introduction · p0025】One adaptive radiotherapy solution utilising cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is the ‘plan of the day’ (POTD) approach, which employs a plan library with varying PTV margins selected based on daily anatomy [1], [2], [8]. POTD has demonstrated PTV reductions of 25–40% whilst improving target coverage [8] and has enabled tumour-focused dose-escalated adaptive radiotherapy (DART) without increased toxicity compared to whole bladder radiotherapy [9].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Feasibility of reduced PTV margins in magnetic resonance image-guided online adaptive radiotherapy for bladder cancer: a personalised approach》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】Patients voided their bladders prior to treatment. Following setup, a daily MRI (MRDAILY) was acquired, and an adaptive workflow was performed. An MRI was acquired during delivery to coincide with treatment completion (MRPOST). Time from MRDAILY to MRPOST was recorded. Offline, target coverage of the clinical target volume (CTV) was visually monitored by comparing MRDAILY and MRPOST images. Images were reviewed by the radiation oncologist (RO) if the CTV was outside of the PTV on the MRPOST. Under RO discretion, margins were personalised to the minimum margin that would have encompassed the CTV and applied online for subsequent fractions. In retrospective analysis, MRPOST CTVs were recontoured, and the adaptive plan recalculated. CTV coverage was deemed acceptable if V95% ≥ 95%. If this objective was not met, the gross tumour volume (GTV) was delineated and the dose reported; coverage was deemed acceptable if GTV V95% ≥ 95%.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Feasibility of reduced PTV margins in magnetic resonance image-guided online adaptive radiotherapy for bladder cancer: a personalised approach》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · p0075】Of the 138 fractions, 119 MRPOST images were available for retrospective analysis, 101 and 18 for 20fr and 6fr cohorts, respectively. For the remaining fractions, MRPOST images were either not acquired or unusable. Overall, CTV coverage was acceptable in 94% (112/119) of fractions (Fig. 4), 93% (94/101) of the 20fr cohort fractions, and 100% (18/18) of the 6fr cohort fractions. The CTV mandatory objective was missed in 7/101 fractions in the 20fr cohort only: three times for patient 2 (twice post-margin increase), twice for patient 4, and once for patients 5 and 6 (Table 2). GTV coverage was acceptable in 6 of these 7 fractions. It was assumed unacceptable without analysis for patient 6 because the disease was multifocal. The incidence in patient 6 occurred after hydration during concurrent chemotherapy administration. For the other instances where the mandatory CTV constraints were not met, no identifiable cause was found.

【Results · p0080】Of the 91 fractions available prior to margin personalisation, 5 mm PTV margins achieved acceptable CTV coverage in 95% (86/91) of fractions, 93% (68/73) and 100% (18/18) of the 20fr and 6fr cohort fractions, respectively. PTV margins were personalised for three patients (Fig. 4), on fractions 9–10. Two patients (patients 2 and 3) increased to 8 mm anisotropic superiorly due to intra-fractional filling. One patient (five) increased to 8 mm in all directions except 10 mm posteriorly, due to variable intra-fractional deformation and filling due to an implant. For these patients, 20/28 fractions were available for analysis before the personalised margins were implemented, 90% (18/20) achieved acceptable CTV coverage. Versus after margin increase, 28/31 fractions were available, 93% (26/28) achieved acceptable coverage.
